documents: Chafik, Holliday, Bacon & Rossby (2022), Irminger Sea is the center of action for subpolar AMOC variability, Geophysical Research Letters 49, e2022GL099133 (published PDF, 11 pages)
pages_convention: printed journal pages (article pages 'n of 11', identical to PDF pages counted from 1); supporting-information figures cited as S plus number

entry.evidence: Thus, our understanding of how the overturning circulation has evolved in the wider North Atlantic cannot be deduced from a single metric

steps.action: Takes from other groups the SST-proxy reconstruction claiming a twentieth-century AMOC slowdown (Caesar et al., 2018).
steps.quote: claimed, largely based on sea-surface temperature proxies, to have slowed down during the twentieth century

steps.action: Poses the question of the subpolar AMOC signature rooted in direct AMOC estimates. The motivation is that SST proxies are poor predictors and that subtropical and subpolar AMOC are incoherent. States the objectives: an OSNAP signature, decadal robustness in a reanalysis, a long-term indicator, and the mechanisms.
steps.quote: these proxies are poor predictors of AMOC strength

steps.action: Assembles existing data: the OSNAP East AMOC time series in density space (2014–2018), EN4 hydrography (1950–2019), CMEMS altimetry, the GloSea5 reanalysis and NCEP/NCAR fields.
steps.quote: We use the maximum transport of the overturning stream function as observed at OSNAP

steps.action: Correlates filtered OSNAP East AMOC with gridded 0–1,000 m density and SSH. Finds the AMOC covaries with high Irminger Sea density and low SSH, with a center of action west of the Reykjanes Ridge.
steps.quote: We find that a strengthening (weakening) of the subpolar AMOC anomaly coincides with anomalous increase (decrease) in upper-ocean density (0–1,000 m)

steps.action: Describes the shoaling of the 27.55–27.7 isopycnals (the AMOC maxima) in the Irminger Sea during AMOC+ compared with AMOC− periods.
steps.quote: The density structure in the Irminger Sea is revealing of a pronounced shoaling of the 27.55–27.7 isopycnals

steps.action: Proposes that Irminger Sea density or SSH can serve as a proxy for interannual-to-decadal and long-term subpolar AMOC change.
steps.quote: may be useful predictors or proxies of interannual-to-decadal and long-term subpolar AMOC changes

steps.action: Checks the premise that GloSea5 AMOC tracks OSNAP East: R = 0.73 over 2014–2018 and comparable interannual standard deviations.
steps.quote: The GloSea5 and OSNAP East AMOC are well correlated, R = 0.73, during the 2014–2018 period

steps.action: Repeats the analysis in GloSea5 over 1993–2019 and finds the same relation. AMOC correlates with the leading SSH PC (R = 0.84). Regressions of SSH and density on AMOC, and on the SSH PC, give nearly identical Irminger Sea centers of action.
steps.quote: We find the same significant relationship between the strength of subpolar AMOC and sea surface height over the past three decades.

steps.action: Keeps Irminger Sea density or altimetric SSH as a proxy for eastern subpolar AMOC variability. Notes that the proxy reveals no mechanism.
steps.quote: can thus be used with confidence to reconstruct and diagnose AMOC variability in the eastern SPNA

steps.action: Asks the origin of Irminger Sea density anomalies, given their spatial disconnect from the maximum buoyancy loss in the Labrador Sea.
steps.quote: In this section, we investigate the origin of the Irminger Sea upper-ocean density.

steps.action: Sets out rivals: local atmospheric forcing, far-field forcing, and ocean circulation. Draws on the cited NAO–Labrador Sea deep-water mechanism and gyre dynamics. Proposes that Labrador Sea buoyancy loss reaches the Irminger Sea via the subpolar gyre.
steps.quote: effects of buoyancy loss in the Labrador Sea have the potential to subsequently impact Irminger Sea upper ocean density via the subpolar gyre circulation

steps.action: Computes the leading EOF of wind-stress curl (NAO-like) and regresses density and net heat flux on its PC. The NAO-like PC explains 40% (interannual-to-decadal) and 67% (multidecadal) of Irminger density variance and leads it by about 1 year.
steps.quote: This NAO-like variability is found to explain 40% (67%) of the observed Irminger Sea density variability on interannual-to-decadal (multidecadal) timescales

steps.action: Varies the smoothing timescale (3-year against 10-year running means) to check that the NAO–Irminger density link holds on both interannual-to-decadal and multidecadal scales.
steps.quote: Same as panel (c) but on multi-decadal time scales (10-year running mean).

steps.action: Sets aside local heat loss as the driver: the largest density changes sit in the Irminger Sea but the strongest heat losses sit in the Labrador Sea.
steps.quote: While positive density changes are largest near the Irminger Sea region, the strongest heat losses are found in the Labrador Sea

steps.action: Designs a test of the advection mechanism suggested by the 1-year lead: backward Lagrangian particle tracking (TRACMASS) in altimetry-derived geostrophic velocities. Particles are released on the Irminger and Iceland Basin sections in 2016.
steps.quote: To investigate this potential mechanism, we perform a backward Lagrangian analysis based on altimetry-derived geostrophic velocities

steps.action: Infers pathways and transit times from the trajectories: Labrador Sea water reaches the Irminger Sea in a median of about 2 years, with first arrivals after a few months.
steps.quote: the median transit time for these particles traced from the Irminger Sea toward the Labrador Sea is about 2 years

steps.action: Compares pathways. Irminger-bound Labrador water travels through the gyre interior, Iceland Basin water through the boundary currents. Subtropical-origin water reaches the Irminger interior only minimally.
steps.quote: these trajectories communicate minimally and only occasionally (possibly through eddy stirring) with the interior Irminger Basin

steps.action: Retains the mechanism: NAO-driven cooling in the Labrador Sea is advected through the gyre interior into the Irminger Sea, preconditioning subpolar overturning.
steps.quote: [...] result provides evidence that water from the interior of the Labrador Sea spreads into the interior Irminger Sea

steps.action: Asks what Irminger Sea density says about long-term subpolar AMOC change. Notes literature cautions that fingerprints may not track long-term AMOC trends.
steps.quote: What Can Irminger Sea Density Tell us About the Strength of the Subpolar AMOC Over the Last 70 Years?

steps.action: Computes the 1950–2019 EN4 Irminger density trend (−0.005 kg/m3 per decade) and scales it with the OSNAP regression slope to a ~2.2 Sv (13%) weakening. A modified Mann-Kendall test finds the trend insignificant at 95%.
steps.quote: this linear trend remains statistically insignificant at the 95% confidence level

steps.action: Sets the estimate against Caesar et al. (2018) and against other reconstructions (Fraser & Cunningham 2021; Rossby et al. 2020; Orvik 2022; Fu et al. 2020; Jackson et al. 2022). Concludes there is no consensus on basin-wide slowdown.
steps.quote: Taken together, we conclude that there is yet no consensus regarding basin-wide North Atlantic slowdown of the overturning circulation.

steps.action: Concludes the Irminger Sea is the center of action for subpolar AMOC variability, with NAO control via the Labrador Sea and gyre. Notes that cold dense upper ocean goes with strong AMOC, challenging the SST-proxy paradigm.
steps.quote: [...] main conclusion of this study is that the Irminger Sea is herein highlighted as the center of action for subpolar AMOC variability.

tree.answer: Nature repeats AMOC/NAO cycles across 2014–2018, 1993–2019 and 1950–2019 records
Relation survives reanalysis period and timescale variation; trend not significant
Irminger Sea kept as center of action; 2.2 Sv weakening suggestive but insignificant
No review file supplied; reviewers only acknowledged

end.claim: Upper-ocean density and SSH in the Irminger Sea track subpolar (OSNAP East) AMOC variability, observed 2014–2018 and supported by reanalysis 1993–2019, making the Irminger Sea the center of action for subpolar AMOC variability.

decisive_move.sentence: Correlating the direct OSNAP East AMOC record with gridded upper-ocean density and SSH revealed the Irminger Sea center of action; without it there is no proxy, no mechanism question and no long-term estimate.

gates.evidence: All data were pre-existing (OSNAP, EN4, altimetry, GloSea5, NCEP/NCAR); no hypothesis directed acquisition. The OSNAP-derived relation could have failed to reappear in GloSea5 (p. 4), and the Lagrangian test could have shown no interior Labrador–Irminger pathway (pp. 7–8). However, the GloSea5 SSH PC agreement is not independent because it assimilates altimetry (p. 4). No hypothesis, threshold or analysis plan is said to have been fixed in advance.

imports.item: Empirical Orthogonal Function analysis (eofs library) of wind-stress curl and SSH
modified Mann-Kendall trend test for autocorrelated data (Hamed & Rao 1998)

novelty_claims.quote: we examine, for the first time, the signature of the overturning in the subpolar North Atlantic (SPNA) that is rooted in direct AMOC estimates
This is the first time that this strong relationship has been observed with direct [...] .

limits: Sub-claims sit at different statuses. The NAO–Labrador Sea–gyre advection mechanism is a best_explanation: correlation, lag and Lagrangian pathways, with local heat loss set aside and subtropical origin shown as minimal. The 70-year weakening of 2.2 Sv (13%) is an estimate_with_resolution that is statistically insignificant at 95%. The challenge to the cold-SST/weak-AMOC paradigm is an interpretation, not tested here. The OSNAP relation rests on about 4 years of filtered data. Inference: applying the 2014–2018 regression slope to 1950–2019 assumes stationarity, which is not tested. Inference: significance levels of the spatial correlations are claimed ('statistically significant relationships') but no test or effective degrees of freedom are reported in the main text. The GloSea5–altimetry SSH agreement is not independent, as the authors note (p. 4). The document does not show what analyses were tried and dropped, the order in which the work was done, or what reviewers requested; no review file was supplied.

disagreements.target: common paradigm from modern and paleo studies that cold North Atlantic SSTs indicate a weakening overturning (SST-proxy reconstructions, e.g., Caesar et al., 2018)
disagreements.support: OSNAP and GloSea5 show that on interannual-to-decadal timescales cold, dense Irminger Sea upper ocean coincides with strong subpolar AMOC.
disagreements.quote: challenges the common paradigm from modern and paleo studies that cold sea-surface temperatures in the North Atlantic are associated with a weakening overturning

disagreements.target: Caesar et al. (2018) estimate of 3 ± 1 Sv AMOC weakening since the mid-twentieth century
disagreements.support: The Irminger density proxy gives a ~2.2 Sv weakening, consistent in magnitude but statistically insignificant because of large interannual and decadal variability.
disagreements.quote: [...] weakening of ∼2.2 Sv or 13% over this period, which is not inconsistent with the Caesar et al. (2018) estimate

disagreements.target: modeling studies in which NAO-driven Labrador Sea deep-water formation drives AMOC change (e.g., Zhang et al., 2019)
disagreements.support: Lagrangian back-tracking and a 1-year lag indicate the Labrador Sea preconditions Irminger waters via the gyre interior rather than dominating subpolar overturning.
disagreements.quote: although the Labrador Sea does not dominate the subpolar overturning, it may play a key role in preconditioning the waters

disagreements.target: claims of a basin-wide North Atlantic AMOC slowdown
disagreements.support: An insignificant subpolar trend here, together with several cited reconstructions finding stability, leaves no consensus.
disagreements.quote: we conclude that no consensus is yet reached regarding basin-wide North Atlantic slowdown of the overturning circulation

alternatives_considered.chosen: wind-stress curl to define the leading EOF mode of atmospheric variability
alternatives_considered.reason: Because of the importance of the wind-stress curl for the basin-scale ocean circulation

alternatives_considered.chosen: AMOC at the eastern part of the OSNAP array (Greenland–Scotland)
alternatives_considered.reason: OSNAP East dominates the mean overturning and its variability
